summary: Feed s135_double to SIEM is degraded: 4.2% TCP packet loss and 76.7% ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic detected. Tool is not overloaded and no other faults found, but drops and unstripped tunnels reduce SIEM detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror or packet broker buffer drops under load - 117 of 2811 TCP packets (4.2%, threshold 1%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating missing data before the SIEM. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is in the visibility path, not tool ingress policing.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete flows and missing events; correlation and alerting miss data, detection coverage reduced and investigations have gaps even though SIEM does not require both directions or full payload.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy vs SPAN which drops under burst load; eliminates the 4% packet loss observed and ensures complete records to SIEM.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker forwarding ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic directly to tool without stripping - 2279 of 2971 frames (76.7%, threshold 10%) are ERSPAN. SIEM sees outer tunnel headers instead of inner original IP/TCP.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM cannot parse inner 5-tuple, application and user context; rules and correlation fail on encapsulated traffic, 76% of traffic is effectively blind for detection despite SIEM not needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker restores original Ethernet/IP headers so SIEM can decode, filter and correlate the inner flows without extra tool load.
